subject: pharmacology
title: Insulin: types, regimens, DKA and hypoglycaemia

steps.tx: **Insulins** sort by kinetics: rapid (**lispro, aspart, glulisine**: meal bolus, pumps), short (**regular**: IV DKA and infusions), intermediate (**NPH**: cloudy, peaks, nocturnal hypoglycaemia), long (**glargine, detemir, degludec**: flat basal, no peak, less nocturnal lows), **premixed** (convenience, rigid). Concentrated U200 and U300 suit resistance; **inhaled Afrezza** (smokers and lung disease banned, spirometry watched) niches. Rotation with lipohypertrophy checks preserves absorption.
steps.say: Meals bolus rapid, nights basaled flat: bolus feeds, basal fasts. Cloudy NPH peaks nightly: lows lurk.

vis.alt: Gantt chart of insulin time profiles: rapid lispro acts from 15 minutes, peaks at 1 hour and lasts 3 to 4 hours; regular acts from 30 minutes, peaks at 2 to 3 hours and lasts 6 to 8 hours; cloudy NPH peaks between 4 and 10 hours and lasts 10 to 16 hours; glargine is flat with no peak and lasts about 24 hours.
vis.caption: Rapid for meals, flat long acting for basal; NPH peaks can cause nocturnal lows.

steps.tx: **Basal bolus** (long basal with rapid meal boluses, carb counting) mimics physiology beating **sliding scale alone** (reactive, hypoglycaemic, hospital harm); correction scales supplement, never substitute. Type 1 always basal (DKA without), type 2 adds basal to orals failing. Dawn phenomenon (morning surge) splits evening basal; Somogyi (nocturnal hypo rebounding) cuts it. Sick day rules (never stop basal, ketones, fluids) prevent DKA.
steps.say: Sliding scale alone harms inpatients: basal always, bolus meals. Dawn rises need basal; Somogyi rebounds cut.

steps.tx: **Diabetic ketoacidosis** (hyperglycaemia with ketonaemia and acidosis, nausea with Kussmaul breathing and fruity breath; infection, missed insulin, SGLT2 euglycaemic triggers) is treated by **fluids first** (saline resuscitation), **IV regular insulin infusion** (fixed weight based, glucose falls, dextrose added), **potassium** (total body depleted despite normal labs; hold insulin under 3.3), bicarbonate only under pH 6.9, trigger hunted. Switch subcutaneous (basal given before stopping infusion) avoids relapse; HHS (no ketones, profound dehydration, higher mortality) fluids more.
steps.say: DKA fluids first, insulin infusion, potassium watched, basal before stopping drip. Euglycaemic SGLT2 DKA fools meters.

steps.tx: **Hypoglycaemia** (**Whipple triad**: symptoms, low glucose, relief on correction; autonomic sweats and tremor versus neuroglycopenic confusion) is treated by **15-15 rule** (15 g fast carbs, recheck 15 minutes) with **glucagon** (unconscious, vomiters) and octreotide for sulfonylurea overdoses (long observation). Impaired awareness (beta blockers mask) needs driving and glucagon co-prescription; **lipodystrophy** rotates sites while pumps with CGM (hybrid closed loop) smooth. Sulfonylurea lows linger days.
steps.say: Confused sweaty diabetic is hypo until glucose proves otherwise: 15 grams, 15 minutes, glucagon if out.
